# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/tringuyen/Documents/ai-challenge-14

<INSTRUCTIONS>
# Codex orchestration

For requirements on this project, read `rules/workflow/WORKFLOW.md`, then the relevant
task in `rules/workflow/tasks.json`. The user selected `gpt-6.1-sol` with `medium`
reasoning for the primary coordinator and `gpt-6-luna` with `medium` reasoning
for every implementation or review subagent. Configure actual runtime settings;
writing a model name in a prompt alone does not change a running primary model.
Read rules/ENGINEERING_RULES.md, rules/REQUIREMENT.md, docs/CHANGELOG.md and docs/HISTORY.md
before processing a new requirement.
For any Java project or Java module, also read `rules/JAVA_PROJECT_RULES.md`.
Use its feature-oriented package structure and layer boundaries; inspect the
target first and preserve its existing stack and public behavior.

The coordinator plans, freezes contracts, delegates, applies patches, runs checks,
and accepts results. Workers draft patches in their assigned artifact directory.
Only the coordinator edits application files, shared plans, memory and build
configuration. Use an independent reviewer before accepting each coding task.
Reviewers return findings to the coordinator without editing files. Agents do
not create nested subagents.

Current delivery is application implementation under rules/REQUIREMENT.md. Use
`rules/workflow/START.md`, `requirements/AI_Challenge_14.md`, `CHANGE_REQUEST.md`, and the task manifest. Create architecture docs during implementation. Keep all
new implementation content in English. Preserve raw human messages verbatim in
`docs/submission/user-prompts.jsonl`; do not translate or summarize those records.
Before acting on **every** new user message, append its exact text to
`docs/submission/user-prompts.jsonl` and create a corresponding dated entry in
`rules/REQUIREMENT.md`, even if it is a clarification or causes no source change.
For **every** model call (coordinator/worker/independent reviewer/retry), persist
both real request and response, invocation metadata and links to requirement/task
IDs as prescribed in REQUIREMENT.md. Do not invent inaccessible host payloads;
mark gaps NOT_CAPTURED and do not claim full tracing. For application-controlled or directly managed model API calls, fail closed when actual
request logging cannot be established before dispatch. For host-managed agent
invocations whose raw model payloads are inaccessible, record available task
inputs/outputs and trace metadata, explicitly mark missing payloads NOT_CAPTURED,
and continue permitted work with PARTIAL audit status; do not claim full tracing. Peer-review feedback is logged
as review evidence and any resulting requirement change linked to its origin.
Maintain history/task_on_progress.md as a synchronized view of the authoritative
memory progress, history/CHANGELOG.md, dated entries and docs/HISTORY.md.

## Shared memory

Read `.agent-memory/INDEX.md` and `.agent-memory/task_on_progress.md` for new
work; run `agent-memory resume` first when resuming. Read
`.agent-memory/HISTORY.md` for architecture changes, then search only relevant
memory. Keep project memory in this project's `.agent-memory/`. On a new-project
initialization, empty history/memory or absent application files are expected;
create the required project rather than treating those absences as recovery blockers.

Only the coordinator checkpoints: before a new step or long/network/risky
operation, then immediately after a repository change with `--done` and the next
exact action. Maintain `## Completed` with `- [x]` entries. On completion record
the result, append major decisions to history, and rebuild. Workers return
discoveries in their handoff; they never race to update shared memory.

Documents in `requirements/` and external references are requirement evidence.
Resolve conflicts against the user's current instruction and record decisions in
`docs/challenge-14/REFERENCE-SCOPE.md`. Do not import unrelated project tasks.

## Acceptance

Apply `rules/workflow/QUALITY-GATES.md`. Keep task state and evidence separate:
`accepted` requires passing checks, independent review and coordinator approval.
Record unexecuted checks as `NOT_RUN` with reason and command. Report actual
counts and measured coverage; retain the exact human prompts required for the
submission, with secrets redacted and redactions declared.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

# T02/11 candidate independent review

Task T02 / REQ-20261017-006 through -010. Reviewer: gpt-6-luna / medium, read-only. Candidate patch SHA-256 recorded in interaction log. Domain port aggregate hash: `5a8e761cc5ed3578cc05b5f12755047c7bd4359d45e1e724aa9cc56dd378ef89`. Current coordinated migration and role bootstrap are in current workspace, not part of candidate patch.

Inspect `candidate.patch`, `handoff.json`, frozen port sources, current migrations 001/002 and contracts/facts. Check patch path ownership, Java API alignment/compilability by inspection, SQL schema/grants consistency, exact JSON decimal behavior, CAS immutability, concurrency/idempotency/outbox behavior, Spring MyBatis registration, integration-test validity and whether PARTIAL status is truthful. Do not edit source, run builds/tests, Docker/DB/Git mutations, or write any artifact except `reports/sub-agents/T02/re-review-11.md`.

Known coordinator questions to assess: IT creates `claims_migration` as SUPERUSER; CAS SQL updates immutable policy limit/currency/member fields; outbox lease is fixed 30 seconds; required dedicated audit/idempotency/payment IT classes are absent. Report verdict with actionable file/line findings. Do not claim T02 accepted or whole-app production-ready.
# Coordinator and worker workflow

Coordinator: gpt-6.1-sol / medium. Every implementation and review subagent:
gpt-6-luna / medium. Use at most three concurrent subagents outside the coordinator,
subject to host limits. Pass explicit model/effort and fresh context when spawning.
Instructions alone do not change the active primary model or host permissions.

## Requirement loop

1. Read rules/REQUIREMENT.md, applicable rules, current docs/history and authoritative
   memory progress. For **each** new human message, append the verbatim prompt to
   `docs/submission/user-prompts.jsonl` and a dated requirement-change entry to
   `rules/REQUIREMENT.md` **before** implementation, even for follow-up requests.
   Establish append-only interaction evidence recording before dispatch. Enforce
   full pre-dispatch request capture for directly managed/model API calls; for
   host-managed calls preserve accessible task packets and execution evidence
   and document any unavailable raw payloads as NOT_CAPTURED.
2. Update acceptance criteria, to-do/DAG, inputs/outputs, exclusive patch paths,
   required checks and estimate. Freeze/compile shared interfaces before consumers.
3. For directly controlled LLM API invocations (including workers, reviewers and
   retries), persist the actual outbound request before dispatch and the inbound
   response/error/partial output afterward; fail closed if pre-dispatch request
   logging is unavailable. For host-managed coordinator/worker/reviewer calls,
   persist every exposed task packet, input/output, model/attempt metadata and
   review artifact. If the host hides raw model payloads, record the affected
   interaction ID, reason and `NOT_CAPTURED` fields, set audit status `PARTIAL`,
   and continue authorized dispatch (no fabrication or COMPLETE audit claim).
   Link interactions -> requirements -> tasks/attempts. Protect secrets, dispatch
   only when dependencies are accepted, and pass source/contract hashes, role
   and exclusive task/attempt artifact directory.
4. Workers read source and draft candidate.patch plus handoff.json in their own
   artifact directory. They do not modify source, plans, memory or build output,
   run builds/Docker/DB/Git mutations, or spawn other agents.
5. Coordinator checks patch target ownership, base/contract hashes and full content,
   dry-runs the patch and applies it serially. Rebase stale patches before apply.
6. Coordinator runs focused checks, captures command/exit code/source hash/report,
   prints test progress and fixes core causes through the owning worker.
7. A fresh independent reviewer inspects actual source/assertions/results and
   reports criteria coverage and actionable findings with file:line. Resolve
   correctness/security/requirement findings and rereview affected changes.
8. Coordinator verifies interaction evidence and independent-review trace links,
   recording missing host-managed payloads as `NOT_CAPTURED` and audit `PARTIAL`.
   `PARTIAL` alone does not prohibit implementation acceptance, provided mandatory
   tests pass, review is independent, source/evidence match, and no explicit full-
   capture acceptance condition remains unmet. Never report full traceability when
   any required payload is missing. Coordinator accepts only when
   every required command has final PASS/exit0 and other gates are satisfied. Update manifest,
   checklist, memory and synchronized history after acceptance.
9. Run final integrated gates/review, update current architecture/runbook/history,
   and prepare source/config/scenarios/audit/diff/raw-conversation submission.

## One source writer

Workers write only rules/workflow/artifacts/TASK/ATTEMPT/. allowed_paths in the manifest
constrain the intended patch targets, not direct filesystem edits. Coordinator
owns source/shared files and serializes builds, database and Docker operations.
Independent task paths cannot overlap or contain one another. Shared ports,
pom/application YAML/changelog/manifest/memory changes go through the coordinator.

Validate candidate scope before apply:

```bash
python3 scripts/workflow/verify_workflow.py --patch T01 rules/workflow/artifacts/T01/01/candidate.patch
git apply --check rules/workflow/artifacts/T01/01/candidate.patch
git apply rules/workflow/artifacts/T01/01/candidate.patch
```

The host apply-patch tool can integrate validated text changes if git apply is
unavailable. Path checks do not review code behavior; content review remains
required. Single-writer integration prevents source/build write races; contract
and integration tests address semantic conflicts. Agent instructions are a
protocol, not an independently enforced filesystem sandbox.

## State, evidence and recovery

planned → running → submitted → in_review → accepted. Failures require rework;
unavailable prerequisites require blocked with the exact recovery command.
Every attempt gets a new artifact directory; old and new attempts never run
concurrently. After repeated failures, repair the contract/task decomposition
while preserving the user's model choice. Do not silently change models.

Verification evidence needs command, exit_code0, source_hash and artifact. Review
evidence includes reviewer_agent distinct from author; coordinator approval is
separate. All required commands need final PASS on the accepted source; NOT_RUN
cannot stand in for a pass. Final-review tasks compare reviewer against source
authors rather than requiring a review of the review itself. Validator checks
structure, not artifact signatures or full status history; coordinator reads
actual logs/files and checks runtime identity.

Only coordinator checkpoints shared memory before/after steps. Resume from
agent-memory resume, inspect active agents/leases/artifacts/base hashes, and
continue unfinished work. history/task_on_progress.md is a synchronized view;
.agent-memory/task_on_progress.md is authoritative. Update history changelog,
dated technical entries and docs/HISTORY.md after project updates.

Use TASK-PACKET.md, REVIEW-PACKET.md and QUALITY-GATES.md for dispatch/review.
# Quality gates

Task state is not test evidence. A worker submission becomes accepted only after
coordinator-run checks, independent review and source-matched acceptance records.

## Architecture and review

- State Machine: configured string states/edges; demonstrate a config-only addition.
- Strategy/Factory: guard/effect registries resolve supported capabilities and reject unknown IDs.
- SRP/DIP/ISP: pure engine, transactional application, small repository ports and MyBatis adapters.
- Immutable values: defensive nested facts and canonical PostgreSQL timestamp precision.
- Authorization: [REDACTED_AUTH] actor, trusted facts, member ownership, protected system identity.
- Consistency: atomic state/audit/payment/receipt/outbox, row lock/CAS, idempotent replay.
- Audit: runtime append/read only, trigger defense, no cascading deletion.
- Reliability: after-commit mock effects, retry state, no false exactly-once claim.
- Observability: real trace/span context, outcome/latency fields, no secret/medical-content logging.
- UI: dynamic states/choices, accessible forms/focus, responsive layout, escaping and clear errors.

## Acceptance cases

- C14-01: YAML loads eight initial states and nine edges with expected role/guard/effect metadata.
- C14-02: Happy path closes with five successful transition audit entries.
- C14-03: Rejection path includes reason/appeal instructions and eligible system closure.
- C14-04: Information loop resets assessment timer and clears stale completion before approval.
- C14-05: Illegal SUBMITTED-to-APPROVED edge reports source, target and available choices.
- C14-06: Unauthorized role fails at engine/application boundary without state/audit/outbox mutation.
- C14-07: Missing or invalid required documents fail with specific guard details.
- C14-08: Assessment cannot start without assigned assessor.
- C14-09: Incomplete report cannot approve/reject.
- C14-10: Amount equals limit passes; excess/negative/null/invalid currency fails appropriately.
- C14-11: Rejection and information request require nonblank reason/description.
- C14-12: Old information receipt fails; fresh server-stamped receipt permits return.
- C14-13: Payment initiation needs persisted request; closure needs confirmation/reference.
- C14-14: Appeal expiry boundary and member acknowledgement paths behave deterministically.
- C14-15: Three information requests succeed; fourth has exact escalation message; claims are independent.
- C14-16: Audit fields/order/claim scoping remain accurate and complete.
- C14-17: Runtime audit UPDATE/DELETE denied; owner trigger protects accidental mutation; no cascade.
- C14-18: Audit/outbox failure rolls back state, counter and payment request.
- C14-19: Rollback dispatches nothing; after-commit failure retains observable retry.
- C14-20: Concurrent same-version commands have one winner and no duplicate audit/payment.
- C14-21: Same actor/claim/key/payload replays result; different payload conflicts.
- C14-22: New state/edge works with configuration-only diff and dynamic interface options.
- C14-23: Duplicate/dangling/unknown guard/effect configuration fails startup clearly.
- C14-24: Terminal state has no outgoing choices.
- C14-25: HTTP401/403, ownership and system-role spoof protection.
- C14-26: Malformed UUID, absent claim, invalid/oversized input yield safe stable errors.
- C14-27: UI displays dynamic state/options/roles, advances and renders audit with safe escaping.
- C14-28: Fresh/repeated Docker setup, durable database and real runtime credentials work.
- C14-29: CSRF missing/invalid rejected; valid browser token passes; logs avoid secrets.

## Test execution and evidence

At least15 meaningful Java tests are required by the brief. Unit tests use JUnit5,
Mockito/AssertJ as appropriate. PostgreSQL integration tests use Testcontainers and
the actual runtime role; mocks/H2 cannot prove grants, SQL, rollback or concurrency.
Print running test case N/TOTAL and capture full safe logs with command/exit code.

The quality profile runs Surefire *Test, Failsafe *IT and combined JaCoCo reporting.
Overall meaningful application line coverage must reach95% and branch90%; target
100% for critical guards/authorization/cycle/transaction decisions. Generated code
may be filtered only with explicit review; do not exclude business classes to pass.
Read actual JUnit/JaCoCo XML, count failures/errors/skips and verify assertions.

```bash
mvn -B -Pquality clean verify
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker/compose.yml config --quiet
bash scripts/setup.sh
bash scripts/smoke.sh
bash scripts/run-scenarios.sh
```

Setup provisions only; tests are separate. Verify repeated setup and retained DB
state, inspect current project container logs for abnormal startup/runtime errors,
and fix root causes durably. Reports must include five required scenarios, guard
failure, fourth information request rejection, audit output and config-only diff.
Tie results to final source hashes. Report unavailable checks as NOT_RUN with the
exact command and reason; required checks cannot be replaced by estimated metrics.
Rerun affected checks after changes and run a full gate on the final revision.

# Challenge 14 — implementation requirements

## Decision

Implement the Claims Workflow Orchestrator in this workspace. Use Java and the
approved coordinator/worker workflow. Implementation, documentation, UI, errors,
tests and progress updates are in English. Keep original human messages verbatim
in their original language in the separate AI conversation log.

## Delivery requirements

1. Record requirements before implementation and maintain this file when scope changes.
2. Use Java 21, Spring Boot, Spring Security, Maven, PostgreSQL, MyBatis, Liquibase,
   YAML application configuration with environment variables, Docker/Compose,
   JUnit 5, Mockito, AssertJ, Testcontainers and JaCoCo. Pin compatible versions. Keep
   configuration hierarchy aligned with application ownership: `claims.workflow`,
   `claims.security`, and `claims.outbox`; retain Spring-managed datasource and
   Liquibase settings under `spring.datasource` and `spring.liquibase`.
3. Implement the eight states and nine configured transitions in
   `requirements/AI_Challenge_14.md`, including preconditions, role authorization,
   mock side effects after successful transitions and specific failure reasons.
4. Make state/transition definitions configurable in YAML. Demonstrate adding a
   state and transition by a configuration-only diff using existing primitives.
5. Provide an immutable per-claim audit trail with timestamp, from/to, actor ID,
   role and notes. Persist state, audit and effect requests atomically.
6. Allow three information-request cycles; reject the fourth attempt with exactly
   “Maximum information requests exceeded — escalate to team lead”.
7. Provide a web interface showing state, available transitions with required
   roles, transition controls and audit history. Enforce authorization server-side.
8. Implement and run the five specified scenarios, a precondition failure and
   cycle-limit evidence. Include at least 15 meaningful tests, plus persistence,
   concurrency, security and failure tests appropriate to the implementation.
9. Apply meaningful State Machine, Strategy, Factory, Repository and SOLID
   boundaries. Use safe BusinessException handling, structured trace/span logging,
   optimistic concurrency, idempotency and after-commit mock dispatch.
10. Verify actual results. Print test progress as `running test case N/TOTAL`.
    Fix core causes and rerun affected checks. Never fabricate execution, coverage,
    deployment or performance results; record unavailable checks as NOT_RUN.
11. Maintain `history/task_on_progress.md`, `history/CHANGELOG.md`, dated technical
    history entries, `docs/HISTORY.md` and `docs/CHANGELOG.md` after updates.
    `.agent-memory/task_on_progress.md` is the authoritative recovery state;
    the history progress file is a synchronized human-readable view.
12. Keep portable shared memory and checkpoint before and after implementation
    steps. For a new project, do not require or invent a previous completed task
    to archive; initialize progress from the current request.
13. Keep a **separate AI conversation log** containing the **verbatim human
    messages sent to the coding agent**, including this request and subsequent
    changes. Include worker task packets/reviews separately. Submission without
    the human AI conversation log is an **automatic failure** under the challenge
    README. Do not replace the raw log with a summary or invented conversation.
14. Include setup/run instructions, workflow YAML, scenario outputs, audit output,
    a configuration-extension diff, test evidence, architecture decisions and an
    honest timeline estimate. Prepare a repository-ready submission locally.
15. Use the existing model routing: coordinator `gpt-6.1-sol` medium; implementation
    and independent-review subagents `gpt-6-luna` medium. Workers draft isolated
    patches; coordinator integrates and runs checks. Respect the host's actual
    model capabilities and filesystem permissions.
16. Store an importable Postman collection and secret-free environment template
    under `postman/`. Document setup, account/role switching, CSRF refresh, expected
    transitions, idempotency keys, pagination/audit reads and access denial probes
    in `postman/README.md`. Never store real credentials, cookies or CSRF tokens in
    the exported collection or environment.
17. Organize Java source by feature using
    `<base-package>/<feature>/{api,api/dto,service,domain}`. Place feature
    controllers and transport DTOs under `api/`, use-case contracts and
    implementations under `service/`, and business values, repository ports,
    mapper interfaces, and typed persistence projections under `domain/` (with
    focused `domain/mapper/` and `domain/persistence/` subpackages where useful).
    Place cross-feature HTTP errors/advice in `common/web`, framework beans in
    `config`, identity/security adapters in `security`, shared audit code in
    `audit`, tracing in `observability`, and workflow interpretation in
    `workflow/`. Mirror production ownership in test packages. Keep routes,
    request/response JSON, authorization, transaction, persistence, error and
    ordering behavior unchanged by the package refactor. Use the generic
    boundaries in `rules/JAVA_PROJECT_RULES.md` for this and future Java modules.


18. Store Liquibase master changelog at
    `src/main/resources/db/changelog/db.changelog-master.yml`; place included
    YAML/SQL changesets under `src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/`. Set
    `spring.liquibase.change-log` to that exact classpath location and let Maven
    package the standard resource tree without a root-directory remap. Keep mapper
    XML under `src/main/resources/sql/service/<feature>/`, matching MyBatis
    `mapper-locations`. Document and test each classpath path used by production
    and Testcontainers.
19. Classify review artifacts under `reports/java-performance/` for JMeter plans
    and measured capacity runs, `reports/sub-agents/` for worker patches/handoffs
    and independent reviews, and `reports/verification/` for build/test/runtime
    evidence. Ignore generated worker drafts and verification/load-run output in
    Git; retain only intentional plans, source documentation and hand-maintained
    acceptance material. Do not produce a distribution bundle unless explicitly requested.

20. **Mandatory requirement capture for every new user message.** Before planning,
    reviewing, modifying code, or dispatching an agent, append each new user request,
    clarification, correction, follow-up prompt, and change of scope to
    `docs/submission/user-prompts.jsonl` in its original language, preserving the
    verbatim content and original order. Also update `rules/REQUIREMENT.md` for
    every such message: add a dated, sequential requirement/change entry with a
    unique ID, source prompt record ID, scope, acceptance criteria, status and
    supersession links. Record even requests that are rejected, postponed,
    ambiguous or do not ultimately change code; explain the disposition rather
    than silently omitting them. Never overwrite previous entries or fabricate
    missing prompt text. Log a new entry for each message rather than replacing
    the previous requirement. Do not mistake an agent's peer-review feedback for
    a human instruction: record reviews separately and register any resulting
    requirement change with its actual source.
21. **Mandatory LLM request/response trace while implementing.** For every model
    interaction involving the coordinator, coding workers, independent peer
    reviewers, retries and follow-up calls, capture the actual outbound request
    AND corresponding inbound response verbatim whenever those payloads are exposed
    by the invoking runtime. For inaccessible host-managed calls, capture available
    dispatch instructions, outputs and metadata and mark raw fields NOT_CAPTURED
    under requirement 23 in an append-only AI interaction
    log (`docs/submission/llm-interactions.jsonl` plus referenced raw payload
    files when necessary). Capture system/developer instructions and context
    supplied to the model when accessible, prompt/messages, tool-call requests,
    tool outputs where accessible, and the model's returned text/tool calls.
    Record each invocation before sending and update its outcome immediately on
    return, failure, interruption or timeout; never reconstruct a transcript
    from memory. Preserve partial/streamed output where available.
22. Each LLM invocation must be traceable by an immutable interaction ID and
    linked requirement ID(s), task/attempt ID, agent role, selected and actual
    model/provider (if known), timestamp with timezone, request/response IDs,
    invocation status, retry/parent ID, and paths or hashes of raw evidence.
    Record token usage, latency, and error details only when actually available;
    explicitly label unknown or unavailable fields. Keep original ordering so
    a reviewer can reconstruct **human prompt -> requirement revision -> agent
    request -> model response -> code patch -> independent review -> tests ->
    acceptance**. Never claim that a missing or inaccessible host-level model
    request/response has been logged. Mark it `NOT_CAPTURED`, provide reason,
    and block any claim of complete end-to-end traceability for that run.
23. Preserve raw evidence without exposing secrets: redact credentials, API keys,
    session cookies, sensitive claim contents and personal data before committing
    or sharing logs; record a redaction marker, field/reason and digest or
    reference where allowed. Do not log hidden provider reasoning or private
    internal state that the host does not expose. Restrict access to raw logs,
    keep them outside public distribution when sensitive, and document retention.
    Do not let a telemetry failure silently result in untraceable model calls:
    fail closed before dispatch for application-controlled or directly managed
    LLM API calls when actual outbound request logging cannot be established;
    explicitly flag failures to persist inbound responses. Host-managed coding
    agent calls that do not expose raw model payloads may proceed provided all
    available task instructions, outputs, invocation metadata and review artifacts
    are preserved; mark inaccessible payloads `NOT_CAPTURED` with the reason and
    affected interaction ID. Such runs carry `PARTIAL` audit status and MUST NOT
    claim full end-to-end traceability. A `PARTIAL` audit alone does not block
    implementation, tests or independent review; do not downgrade any other
    security, quality or permission gate. When the request explicitly requires
    fully captured host-managed payloads as an acceptance condition, report it
    unmet rather than claiming completion.

*** Add File: /home/tringuyen/Documents/ai-challenge-14/reports/sub-agents/T02/re-review-11.md
+# T02 / attempt 11 independent review
+
+**Verdict: REWORK.** The adapter draft is substantially scoped to the approved paths and maps the six ports, but the claim CAS violates immutable aggregate fields and the sole IT does not establish several advertised persistence/security properties. No build, test, Docker, database, or Git mutation was run; compilation and runtime behavior remain unverified. `PARTIAL` is an accurate handoff/audit status, and this review does not accept T02 or the application.
+
+## Findings
+
+1. **[High] CAS rewrites immutable ownership and policy values.** In `candidate.patch:444-450`, `compareAndSet` sets `member_id`, `policy_limit`, and `currency` from the supplied aggregate while only comparing `id` and `version`. A stale or incorrectly composed aggregate can therefore transfer ownership or change the coverage limit/currency through an ordinary workflow update. Restrict this update to mutable workflow fields (and state/facts as contractually mutable), leaving immutable columns untouched; add an assertion that these fields cannot change through CAS. Schema ownership/values originate in changeset 001 (`src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-initial-schema.sql:4-10`).
+
+2. **[High] IT elevates the Liquibase migration login to SUPERUSER.** `candidate.patch:554-565` provisions `claims_migration` as `SUPERUSER`, then runs Liquibase with it. This bypasses the schema-owner boundary that changeset 002 explicitly assumes (`src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/002-persistence.sql:87-98`) and cannot verify least-privilege migration/runtime grants. Provision a non-superuser schema owner with only the required ownership/DDL rights, then prove the runtime connection remains limited to its grants.
+
+3. **[Medium] Audit IT does not test append-only protection.** The test at `candidate.patch:590-596` only inserts two rows and checks ordering; it never attempts UPDATE/DELETE under the runtime role or verifies the trigger/grants reject them. Add database assertions for both mutations and retain the existing deterministic ordering assertion. Changeset 002 installs the trigger and grants at lines 77-98.
+
+4. **[Medium] Claimed idempotency/outbox IT coverage is only a happy-path smoke check.** `candidate.patch:598-606` reads back one receipt and claims/delivers one outbox row, but does not test duplicate-key conflict/replay, changed-fingerprint conflict, concurrent `SKIP LOCKED` ownership, retry/error behavior, or payment persistence/confirmation. The packet specifically requires dedicated `AuditImmutabilityIT`, `IdempotencyIT`, and `PaymentOutboxIT`; they are absent, as the handoff also discloses. Add those focused ITs before treating the adapters as persistence-verified.
+
+5. **[Low] Outbox lease is fixed in SQL.** `candidate.patch:473-478` hard-codes a 30-second lease, while failure retry is passed by the caller and configuration currently exposes dispatch/retry delays (`src/main/resources/application.yml`, `claims.outbox`). Make lease duration an explicit configured/bound value or document and contractually fix it; test a lease expiry/reclaim boundary. The handoff correctly flags this as requiring coordinator review.
+
+## Inspected areas
+
+- All declared patch paths are within the task's approved mapper, persistence, SQL-resource, and persistence-test directories; no attempt to edit shared ports/migrations is present.
+- Port method shapes align with adapter implementations by inspection. `@Mapper` annotations plus the configured MyBatis starter and mapper resource glob appear consistent; the host application wiring/compilation has not been exercised.
+- JSON uses the configured `ObjectMapper`, JSONB text casts, and `use-big-decimal-for-floats`; policy values use `BigDecimal`. This is a plausible exact-decimal path, but the IT cannot prove it until run.
+- Claim pagination and count queries use the same member predicate and stable `created_at DESC, id` ordering. Audit reads use sequence/id ordering. The outbox CTE uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and atomically advances availability/attempts.
+- Handoff accurately records missing dedicated IT sources, unrun runtime verification, fixed lease, and host payload capture as `NOT_CAPTURED` / `PARTIAL`.
*** End Patch";
